assets.generation_summary: A pulse rather than a melody: a 62 Hz tick every half second that doubles in rate under the two numbers, over a 41 Hz drone. Ramps to nothing at 35.8-36.9s and never returns.
Narration over the bed with ducking at 0.2 during speech.

DESCENT. Near-black frame, faint instrument grid breathing at the edges. A single cyan trace enters from the top edge and keeps travelling downward through the whole shot - it is never stopped, never blocked. On 'They add one', the word BLOCK, set small in white above the trace, is struck through and the word ADD takes its place without the layout shifting. Hand-authored Remotion scene; no stock t
Assets-gate review still.

MIRROR. The cyan trace is joined by an amber trace that is its exact vertical mirror, drawn on in real time as the narration says 'flips the wave upside down'. On 'The two meet' the pair slide together; on 'Both disappear' they collapse into one flat hairline and the grid dims. This is the only appearance of the canonical cancellation diagram in the video, and it is over in six seconds.
Assets-gate review still.

THE TURN. The hairline is wiped away and the frame is briefly empty. Heavy white type, left-aligned, low in the frame: 'That part is easy.' It holds, then is replaced by the geometry of the rest of the video - a microphone glyph at the top of the frame, an ear at the bottom, and a deliberately unexplained gap between them. Intended render treatment is a bespoke title beat, not the stock TextCard c
Assets-gate review still.

THE RACE. A microphone at the top, an ear at the bottom, and a cyan pulse that leaves the microphone and travels down the gap toward the ear. In the right margin a microsecond counter starts running and does not stop for the rest of the video. The pulse arrives before anything has been drawn to answer it - the frame is losing the race and the viewer sees it.
Assets-gate review still.

DIMENSIONED. The same mic-to-ear axis, now annotated like an engineering drawing: extension lines, arrowheads, and the gap called out in centimetres, with the time that distance actually buys set beneath it in monospace. Static composition, animated only by the ticking counter and the dimension lines drawing themselves on.
Assets-gate review still.

TOLERANCE. Back to the two traces, now with a thin tolerance band drawn around the amber one and labelled 40 microseconds in monospace. Inside the band the traces still cancel - the flat line holds. The band is visibly narrow against the width of one wave cycle, which is the point.
Assets-gate review still.

SLIP. The label rolls to 100 microseconds and the amber trace slides out of register with the cyan one. The flat line breaks apart and residue comes back into the frame - the cancellation visibly fails, and it fails by an amount the viewer can see is small. The hero shot of the video: the argument is won here, in picture, not in narration.
Assets-gate review still.

THE BAND. The frame turns into a frequency axis running the full height of the vertical format, low frequencies at the bottom. Cancellation floods up from the bottom as a cool field and stops dead partway up. The narration names the engine at the moment the flood covers the low end.
Assets-gate review still.

ABOVE THE LINE. The same axis. Everything above the ceiling keeps moving - a restless band of activity where speech lives, drawn in white so it reads as untouched rather than as an enemy. The covered band is labelled once, in monospace, against the axis. On 'There is no time' the whole frame stops moving except that band.
Assets-gate review still.

STILLNESS. Everything stops. One flat hairline across the centre of the frame, the microsecond counter frozen mid-count, the grid holding for the only time in the video. The closing line sets small and low. The title appears once, in the corner, and the frame does not move again. No end card, no subscribe prompt, no logo animation.
Assets-gate review still.

metadata.note: Every visual in this video is drawn by the project's own Remotion composition.
